items.label: Amkor Technology Q2 FY2026 (07-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: RECORD Q2 2026, well above its own guidance: net sales $1.9B

set.signal: RECORD Q2 2026, outperforming the high end of guidance (CFO Megan Faust): net sales $1.9B (+26% YoY, +13% QoQ); gross margin 16.8% (14.2% in Q1 and 12.0% a year ago); operating income $200M (10.5% margin vs 6.0% in Q1); net income $174M; EPS $0.70; EBITDA $400M. Both advanced and mainstream revenue increased year-on-year (mainstream: fifth consecutive quarter of YoY growth). Packaging 88% / test 12% of sales. Customer concentration easing: top-ten customers 66% of sales (from 72% a year ago). End markets: communications 42%, COMPUTING 22% (data center, infrastructure, PC/laptop, storage), automotive/industrial 22%, consumer 14% - CEO Kevin Engel cites RECORD REVENUE IN COMPUTING AND AUTOMOTIVE & INDUSTRIAL, and says H1 2026 'expanded strategic partnerships across the semiconductor ecosystem, advanced key customer programs in AI and HPC, and continued the expansion of our Advanced packaging and test capacity'. Q3 2026 guide: net sales $1.95-2.05B, gross margin 18.5-19.5% (further expansion), EPS $0.72-0.82. FY2026 capex reiterated at ~$2.5-3.0B. Cash + short-term investments $2.5B against $2.5B total debt.

items.reason: The prior guidance ranges ($1.75-1.85B, 14.5-15.5% GM, $0.42-0.52 EPS) appear in neither the call nor the same-day release saved under this label; the CFO says only 'outperforming the high end of our guidance'.
items.evidence: Amkor delivered record second quarter revenue of $1.9 billion, a sequential increase of 13%, outperforming the high end of our guidance.

items.label: Amkor Technology Q2 FY2026 (07-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: TWO LANDMARK PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS REPRICE AMKOR'S ROLE IN AI PACKAGING.

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: TWO PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENTS IN AI PACKAGING (CEO Kevin Engel). (1) A 10-YEAR ADVANCED PACKAGING AGREEMENT WITH TSMC - 'a framework to expand advanced packaging and test capacity while strengthening the U.S. semiconductor supply chain', combining TSMC's leading-edge wafer fabrication with Amkor's advanced packaging and test to give customers 'more integrated manufacturing solutions, spanning advanced silicon fabrication through advanced packaging and test' and to build 'a more resilient semiconductor ecosystem in Arizona'. (2) A MULTI-YEAR STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP WITH NVIDIA covering advanced packaging and test 'supporting NEXT-GENERATION AI INFRASTRUCTURE', aligning long-term technology roadmaps and supporting expansion of advanced packaging capacity. In Q&A the CEO described the NVIDIA structure as 'a prepayment that would basically be received in 2027 and return back to the customer as we provide the services in the U.S.', with agreement length 'between five to 10 years' and NO step-function increase in Amkor R&D (Amkor typically spends 3%-5% of its capital on R&D). He added that such agreements are NOT US-only - 'we have several ASIA-BASED agreements' building 'a high level of confidence in our long-term loading in our Asia facilities' - and that customer engagements increasingly include 'longer planning horizons, capacity alignment discussions, and other forms of investments', a level of collaboration and visibility 'meaningfully different from previous industry cycles'.
set.figure: 10-year TSMC agreement; multi-year NVIDIA partnership with a prepayment received in 2027 (5-10 yrs)

items.reason: The $1.5B prepayment is the analyst's number (Craig Ellis), never stated or confirmed by management; 'reprice Amkor's role' was the enricher's framing.
items.evidence: With that, the longevity of the agreement can fluctuate a bit, but we would expect it to be between five to 10 years.

items.label: Amkor Technology Q2 FY2026 (07-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: THE MEMORY SHORTAGE IS NOW VISIBLY DENTING PHONE BUILDS AT THE OSAT LEVEL.

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: MEMORY SUPPLY IS WEIGHING ON PHONE BUILDS AT AMKOR. Communications (Amkor's largest end market) grew 6% sequentially on double-digit iOS growth, while ANDROID REVENUE FELL 20% 'reflecting the impact of MEMORY SUPPLY DYNAMICS' (CFO Megan Faust). Q3 communications is guided DOWN high-single-digits sequentially - 'a departure from the typical seasonal patterns' - on three factors: the SiP transfer to Vietnam, 'ongoing memory supply constraints', and build-pattern changes; CEO Kevin Engel put the market-driven part at 'probably about 50%' and the SiP move at the other 50%. Q4 is also not expected to see the usual second-half lift ('maybe a little bit of softness... We wouldn't expect to see a significant lift like we typically would in the second half'), and for one SiP application space the headwind is 'not a one-quarter dynamic. It's probably going to extend into Q4 and even into the first half of next year' (CEO). The CEO also cited memory pricing 'and potentially how that affects the end market, the selling of the phones per unit volume', noting that GfK and Gartner 'would expect unit volumes to be down this year'.

items.reason: Restores the CEO's hedges ('probably about 50%', 'potentially') that the entry had rewritten as facts; attributes each statement to its speaker.
items.evidence: I'd say that's probably about 50% of what we're seeing from a typical type of seasonal Q3 lift. The other 50% would be driven by, again, this SiP move.
